summary: Intermittent dedicated-pool throughput sag from mixed-precision micro-bursting and NVLink handshake stalls
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NimbusMaps) reports intermittent dedicated-pool throughput degradation for their reserved cluster during business hours (10:30–11:15 PDT). Impact: p50 throughput dropped ~30% and p99 latency doubled for batched generate requests. Behavior is bursty and correlates with many short-lived small-batch inference streams from a single tenant.

Impact:
- Customer-facing API calls experienced higher token-completion latency; some requests hit caller-side timeouts.
- Autoscaler reacted by spinning additional nodes, then later reclaimed them causing oscillation and temporary capacity shortfall.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: reserved-cluster-id: rc-42-nimbus
- Region: us-west-2 (g4dn/g5 mix)
- Serving runtime v2.14.0 (kernel selector v1.9)
- Autoscaler v1.8.2 with cooldown=60s, predictive mode enabled

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Customer issues many concurrent short streams (~1000/s) of <=3-token prompts with mixed-precision model variants (fp16 and q4_0).
2) Requests multiplex across GPUs and force frequent attach/detach cycles.
3) NVLink/H2 handshake logs spike and small DMA transfers become serialized.
4) Serving runtime falls back to CPU-attached batches for a fraction of requests, increasing per-token latency and causing autoscaler to add capacity.

Relevant logs (excerpts):
- 2026-03-13T10:32:12Z [allocator] attach_request tenant=nimbus tenant_conn=3421 latency_ms=12
- 2026-03-13T10:32:12Z [nvlink] handshake_start gpu=0x3a err_rate=0.02
- 2026-03-13T10:32:12Z [nvlink] handshake_retry gpu=0x3a retry=2
- 2026-03-13T10:32:13Z [runtime] short_stream_fanout tenant=nimbus streams=1120 fallback_cpu=23
- 2026-03-13T10:33:05Z [autoscaler] scale_out reason=high_p99 predicted_needed=4 cooldown_remaining=3s

Investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis: a noisy tenant was creating many extremely short micro-batches with mixed-precision flags that triggered suboptimal kernel selection and increased NVLink contention.
- Verified that nvlink error/retry counters spike during the window and correlate with fallback_cpu metric.
- GPU telemetry shows elevated PCIe transfer queue depth on affected nodes, not a full GPU memory issue.
- Autoscaler predictive model over-allocated due to transient p99 spikes; cooldown prevented immediate reclaiming and led to transient imbalance in slot availability.
- No driver crashes or node restarts observed.

Customer communication (summary):
- 2026-03-13 11:00 PDT: Notified customer we are investigating; asked for recent request patterns and sample request IDs.
- Customer provided a sample trace: req-gn-98765 and a list of short prompt batches.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Throttled their short-stream concurrency at the edge for this dedicated pool (rate limit applied to tenant nimbus: 350 concurrent streams).
- Increased autoscaler cooldown to 120s for rc-42-nimbus to avoid oscillation while we stabilize kernel selection telemetry.
- Toggled kernel-selector hint to prefer larger vectorized kernels for q4_0 on affected nodes (canary change on 2 nodes).

Hypothesis and root-cause (current):
Mixed-precision micro-bursts from a single tenant cause frequent tiny DMA transfers across NVLink that serialize on hardware when coupled with heterogeneous GPU types. The serving runtime's kernel selection combined with short-lived attach/detach cycles causes some requests to fallback to CPU execution path. That fallback, in turn, drove p99 spikes that caused the autoscaler to overreact, producing temporary capacity churn and net throughput loss.

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering (runtime) to add telemetry to flag "nvlink-retry -> fallback_cpu" causality and surface per-tenant counters (assigned: Marco Diaz, ETA 2026-03-18).
- Scheduler to add a short-window affinity pin for small-stream-heavy tenants to reduce attach/detach churn (assigned: Leila Haddad, ETA 2026-03-20).
- Autoscaler tuning: evaluate predictive-model threshold to ignore single-minute p99 spikes for dedicated pools (assigned: SRE team, ETA 2026-03-22).
- Long-term: guidance for customers on best practices for high-rate short-stream workloads (support doc draft) and an SDK helper to batch short requests client-side (assigned: DevRel, ETA 2026-04-05).

Resolution notes (in-progress):
- Canary kernel-selector tweak reduced fallback_cpu from 23 -> 2 on the two canary nodes during the next replication window.
- Rate-limit and cooldown prevented immediate recurrence; awaiting more data after 24-hour monitoring window.

Workarounds provided to customer:
- Recommended client batching to combine short prompts into slightly larger batches (2–8 tokens aggregated) and to use a single precision variant (prefer fp16) per connection.
- Temporary concurrency cap applied (350 streams) until affinity and kernel telemetry shipped.

References and links:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/uid/throughput/rc-42-nimbus
- NVLink counters dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/uid/hw-nvlink
